OK so I see this argument everywhere about which is better, and most people lean towards FO3 story wise and F:NV mechanic wise. And while this is only a matter of opinion, I want to explain why I think F:NV also excels in its world building versus FO3 and why its my favorite game of all time.

So since my explanation is ridiculously long, I'm going to break it down into a couple comments posted down below. In each comment I will explain why I love certain things about FNV and why I think FO3 failed to achieve in that aspect.

Story

Factions

Characters

Factions

For starters, the world feels more accurate in FNV. The great war happened 200 years ago, but in FO3 it feels like it only happened 50 years ago. Cities are sparse, and there are no established factions except the incredibly bland Brotherhood of Steel and the slightly more interesting Enclave. The dangerous and hostile environments are great, but do not fit correctly in the established world IMO.

So for the factions on FO3, we have the BoS which is designed to be the good karma faction. They are friendly and badass, and seem to be 100% good. This is highly inaccurate from the established Fallout lore, in which the BoT is actually much more hostile and pretentious to pretty much everyone outside their order. They steal important technologies from settlements and are stunting the regrowth of civilization. Also, the main story shoehorns you into supporting them pretty much no matter what.

Then we have the Enclave, which is actually closer to the original BoS than the BoS is in FO3. They are shown pretty much as 100% evil, attacking you and hatching schemes and such. They even kill your dad in a "dispute" in which both parties are trying to accomplish the same exact thing (wtf?). Probably the most interesting part of this faction is John Henry Eden, who ends up being a gray character instead of just black or white.

Minor shout out to the Outcasts, for what little they do. And that is all there is to FO3: black or white.

OK now let's talk about factions in FNV, which we have the BoS, Enclave, NCR, Caesar's Legion, Powder Gangers, Great Khans, Mr House, the and Boomers. None of these factions are black or white, they are all inbetween with various traits.

The BoS in FNV is exactly how it should be: hostile and damaging to everyone outside their faction. They steal technology from settlements by gunpoint, and even took control of a power plant and cut off power to New Vegas and the surrounding settlements. They rob travelers at gunpoint and steal any technology they have. They clash with the NCR because of this, and end up losing a major battle against them. When you meet them the first time, they steal your equipment and strap a bomb collar to your neck until you do whatever chores they want you to do.

The New California Republic (NCR) is basically the government of California expanded to a federal level and spreads several states in western USA. They support the old government ideals and provide protection and freedom for all its citizens. They make efforts to build settlements and expand their technology by growing crops, building water lines, and establishing electrical power. They are unfriendly to existing factions or tribes that refuse to submit to their jurisdiction, and one event lead to the slaughtering of many civilians of the Great Khans tribe. The NCR clashes with the BoS and CL over control of important territories.

Caesar's Legion is basically a massive army of tribals formed into a survival-of-the-fittest faction. Caesar, the leader, believes that the old world's government is responsible for the destruction of the world, and wants to avoid history from repeating. The legion goes town-to-town, state-by-state, killing and enslaving anyone who is corrupt. Settlements that are honest are protected by the legion and left to continue their daily routine. The Legion even sabotages NCR's attempts to gain nuclear weaponry. Caeser himself is a brilliant man, and although his faction is harsh, the successful results are hard to argue.

I can go into detail with the remaining factions, but they all follow the same suit of having depth behind their actions in game, and different reason to support each.

Ive only played through the game once and have no idea how you can view the Brotherhood as "hostile". I dont know how you can end up with a bomb strapped to your neck but thats not what happened to me. I met with this one girl halfway to New Vegas and she told me she was a scribe and we should head back to the bunker. So I did that and after letting me in they said they desperately needed my help overthrowing their leader and saving them, and were overally really friendly. As far as I understood it they also wanted to keep the solar plant out of the hands of the NCR because they knew it could somehow be used as a weapon, and didnt want its power to be used in the war against the Legion.

I think if there is any faction that was really welcoming and peaceful towards me it was them.

That would be because you had Veronica with you, who is a member of the BoS and the only one that is nice to strangers (and viewed as a heretic by her peers). She openly admits the BoS is lost in its ways and doomed if it doesn't change. If you approach the bunker without Veronica (or without meeting her) they will capture you and basically hold you hostage. If you approach wearing NCR gear, they will kill you on sight. In fact if you do the BoS story line, they will attempt to kill you and Veronica after some time.

The power plant Helios 1 does hold the secret weapon Archimedes II but the NCR would have never had to take the plant from the Brotherhood if they allowed power to access settlements, or possibly even try cooperation with the NCR. The Followers of the Apocalypse realized this, hence why they work side-by-side with the NCR inside Helios 1. The secret of the weapon is kept from the NCR because they would try to use it against Caesar's Legion, which depending on who you side with, could be a good or bad outcome.

For me it wouldnt really matter if they used it on the Legion since I chose to establish yesman and myself as rulers of Vegas. I stopped playing when I had to fight the Legatus in Caesars camp since no matter what I just couldnt beat him with all my powerarmor and endgame sniper rifles :(

Story

OK so many people support FO3 over FNV for the story, and although I can see the reasoning behind it, iIMO FO3 has a pretty bad manufactured story that is highly linear and artificial motivation.

In FO3 you follow your dad across the wasteland because you love him and maybe want answers. Maybe you don't care about your dad, that's fine, but you will never finish the main story then. You follow him and find out he's trying to restore purified water to the DC wasteland by fixing a purifier. Then the Enclave show up and demand your dad fixes the purifier. Your dad refuses to fix the purifier even though that is his goal and instead decides to kamikaze suicide the Enclave. The Enclave get pissed and capture you so you don't fuck with them while they try to fix the purifier. You escape and possibly blow up the Enclave base, and rally with the BoS to defeat the Enclave and fix the purifier. Do you see how stupid this is? Everybody wants the same thing, and the conflict is manufactured.

Meanwhile in FNV, the story begins with a platinum poker chip. Your character is a mostly harmless courier who is "killed" for his package, and then saved by a local doctor and the mysterious cowboy robot Victor. Some quick dialogue with the townsfolk and Victor and you can immediately tell there is something bigger going on with the chip. Now here's the beauty in this, you can say "ehh fuck the chip" and ignore it completely, and still complete the main story through other factions. The game points you to head to New Vegas, and introduces you to all the major players along the way. You interact with them, see their motivations, and by the time you get to New Vegas, you can choose to support one of them, or fuck them all and make your own attempt to control New Vegas and defeat all the other factions. Now that is freedom.

The big thing to note is the different developers of each game. Bethesda developed FO3 and they strongly prefer linear storylines that mirror what you would see in a movie or read in a book. Obsidian developed FNV and they strongly prefer old fashioned RPG stories that the player can greatly influence or change completely. FNV gives you all the strings, and lets you choose which threads to follow.

But wait, there's more!

Continuing the theme of old fashioned RPG stories, the game DLCs tell the story of several other characters that are largely important and referenced several times in the vanilla story. One instance is with the Burning Man, or Joshua Graham. Speaking with the NCR or Legion will teach you the story of Joshua Graham, who was a great general of Caesar's Legion and basically the most badass warrior ever. You can hear stories of his different exploits and basically about how unstoppable this guy was. However, when Caesar's Legion lost the first battle of Hoover Dam, Caesar had Joshua covered in pitch, lit on fire, and thrown off the Grand Canyon*. Caesar then forbid anyone from speaking his name, and henceforth he is only remembered as the Burning Man. Turns out he survived all of this, and when you meet Joshua for the first time after learning all his legends, his character does not disappoint.

There are other examples with this with Father Elijah and Ulysses, which are equally interesting. In fact Ulysses' entire story is so fantastic it changed the way I view video games as a whole. I won't spoil it here but the build up from the entire game, and all the DLCs ending with "The Lonesome Road" just perfectly climaxes with his revelation.

"Home isn't where you're born into this world. You taught me that. Part of your message, whether you meant it or not. Can be a place of mind, a moment where you know who you are, the history of it. And they can be places you breathe life into."

I would upvoat all of you for effort... and because they're BOTH my favorite games of all time.

but, I can't.

Characters

So FO3 has some very memorable characters, which I do love. I very distinctly remember Dad, Butch, Moriarty, Sydney, Three Dog, John Henry Eden, Tenpenny, and Eulogy Jones. And as fun as these characters were, there wasn't any depth to them (save for John Henry Eden) and mostly they just send your ass on fetch quests. I'm sure there's some exceptions that I can't think of off the top of my head, but the fact I can't remember them ties into my issue with FO3 characters.

Meanwhile in FNV characters worth mentioning are Victor, Sunny Smiles, Deputy Beagle, ED-E, Boone, Veronica, Cass, The King, Fisto, Rex, Benny, Arcade, Mr House, Caesar, Joshua Graham, Ulysses, Dog/God, Dr Mobius and his Robo Scorpion Army, Motorhead, Father Elijah, Raul, Rhonda on Black Mountain, Yes-Man, Mr Fantastic, and Legate Lanius. All of these characters are very interesting IMO, and each has their own piece to the greater setting that is FNV. Even still there are more characters that I can picture but can't think of their names. So not every character above has a ton of depth, but I would say about 75% of them do. The companions have interesting side quests and character development depending on how the quests go.

What's equally brilliant about FNV is you can complete the main story line and miss pretty much every character on that list except Mr. House and Legate Lanius. FO3 forces you into meeting their very specific characters like Dad, Three Dog, Moriarty, and the BoT people whom I can't name. Its possible to skip some of them if you have played the game before and instead know exactly where to find Dad.

@lamphammer: with the advent of better, less viscous, less dirty oils, it is true that you are able to run them for longer. There are two components to an oil change, however; the oil and the oil filter must be changed.

The oil filter arguably has to work less with cleaner oils. Regardless, they have not benefited nearly as much in the way of technological improvement, relative to the actual oil. Quality-made oil filters will allow you to run more miles in between changes, but it is very likely that even with a quality filter you will need to have an oil change before the life of your oil has run out, due to the filter needing replacement.

I look at it this way: Frequent oil changes are a nice insurance policy. Oil filters, when clogged, have a large chance of completely destroying your engine due to lack of oil pressure. For this reason, even with quality oil and a quality filter I myself would not go more than 10k between changes.

Oil, even synthetics, break down with use. This changes the viscosity which increases strain on the oil pump and seals and increases the friction coefficient of the lubricated parts. Also, the oil gets carbon buildup from spent fuel on the cylinder walls. Over time the trace amounts that pass the seals build up in the oil itself. Yes, oil absolutely needs to be changed. Why do you think oil would be clear going in and black coming out if it didn't wear out over time?
